summary: Owner isolation is preserved and emulator-tested across every private collection. No rules were loosened. Live Firebase project/edition and deployment are unverified. This is a code review, not a production security certification.

findings.issue: Authorization uses request.auth.uid against the path UID; no owner-written profile role grants authority. Cross-user get/list/create/update/delete tests added.
findings.recommendation: Retain these regressions and verify the identical rules in the selected real project.

findings.issue: Profile and Meg schemas are owner-only but broadly writable; some bounded lists/maps lack per-member validation.
findings.recommendation: Derive strict backward-compatible schemas from actual records and migrate/test them separately before broad public exposure.

findings.issue: Unauthenticated create is intentional, but string/nested payload sizes and submission frequency need tighter abuse controls.
findings.recommendation: Add bounded payload validation and a trusted anti-abuse entry point before publicly promoting the waitlist.

findings.issue: Tests cover owner profile, cycle, check-in, Diet, Strength and Meg reads/writes/deletions plus Meg history listing and feedback.
findings.recommendation: Complete real-project sign-up, restoration, password delivery and deletion acceptance testing with disposable accounts.
